messages:
elaine: Noticing host-proxy p99 decode up ~9% after kernel-selector rollout. Canary shows the same. Probable host-side parse/tokenize + streaming chunking.
mohit: Repro locally. Flamegraph top: parse_frame, tokenize_inline, syscall:read. Many small writes from http2/gRPC clients.
ryan: paste perf top?
mohit:
```
  29% parse_frame
  19% tokenize_inline
  12% syscall:read
   8% memmove
   6% kernel_selector::choose
```
elaine: kernel_selector picked a fallback kernel for short seqs (matmul_v2_fallback) that does alignment memcopies. Combined with many tiny frames, we get worse host CPU and worse kernel choices.
sam: kvcache hitrate steady (~81%). This looks ingress/parse related.
perf-bot: ALERT host-proxy p99 +0.09s since 2026-03-21T22:40Z (kernel-selector flag flip).
ryan: Quick mitigation candidates: prefer matmul_v1 for seq<32; increase smallwrite batching timeout 3ms->6ms; enable ingress writev coalesce for http2/gRPC.
mohit: microbench: aggressive low-latency flush gives batch sizes 1-2 and hurts throughput ~10%.
sam: local writev coalesce experiment reduced syscalls ~38% and sys CPU ~11%.
elaine: I'll roll a canary patch with kernel priority flip + coalesce + timeout bump. Deploying at 2026-03-22T09:12Z.
ryan: follow-ups: add selector seq-bucket unit tests, add perf harness for http2 smallwrites, run kvcache stress to ensure no regressions.
mohit: opening PR with benchmark, tagging @sam for writev review.
elaine: thanks :thumbsup: monitoring canary for 24h then promote if stable.
